title: Maximum Profit from Valid Topological Order in DAG
summary: Given a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, where edges[i] = [ui, vi] denotes a directed edge from node ui to vi, and each node has a score in the array score, calculate the maximum profit by processing nodes in a valid topological order.
statement: Given a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, where edges[i] = [ui, vi] denotes a directed edge from node ui to vi, and each node has a score in the array score, calculate the maximum profit by processing nodes in a valid topological order. The profit is the sum of each node's score multiplied by its position in the order. A valid topological order ensures that for every directed edge u → v, node u precedes v.
constraints: The graph is a DAG with n <= 22 and positive node scores.
Every edge u->v requires u before v; positions are one-based.
Maximize sum(score[node]*position) over valid topological orders.
hints: With at most 22 nodes, the set already placed is a complete state; its size fixes the next multiplier.
Encode each node’s prerequisites as a bitmask and perform maximum-profit subset DP.
For every reachable mask, append each unchosen node whose prerequisite mask is contained, adding score times the next position.
Every transition preserves topological validity, and every valid order corresponds to one complete sequence of transitions.
editorial: Every transition preserves topological validity, and every valid order corresponds to one complete sequence of transitions.

tests.explanation: After node zero, placing score three before score six yields profit 25.
